title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 98
paragraphs: While Xerxes was doing this, he sent a messenger to the Persians to announce the calamity that had befallen them. Now there is nothing mortal that completes a journey with more speed than these messengers — so ingeniously has this been devised by the Persians. They say that for as many days as the entire journey takes, that many horses and men are stationed at intervals along the route, each man and horse assigned for a day's ride. Neither snow, nor rain, nor heat, nor darkness of night prevents each one from completing his assigned task with the utmost speed. The first rider delivers the message entrusted to him to the second, and the second to the third, and so on it goes, passed from hand to hand, like the torch-race among the Greeks which they hold for Hephaistos. This kind of horse-relay the Persians call the angareion.
